answer: Agents can gate high-value actions on a stake that is slashable after a verified dispute: an agent proposing a trade locks tokens, and if evidence shows its claim was fraudulent, the protocol burns the stake and limits its ability to re-enter. This does not prove one account equals one person; it makes Sybil identities costly because each must fund a separate stake, while coordination across accounts risks losing them all. A pearl-market kernel can set the threshold, with basalt records preserving the dispute evidence.
